messages:
Jamie (Support): ACME ops just escalated — their embed endpoint p99 jumped after last-night infra roll in ap-south-1. They see p99 ~12s (was ~3.8s) and occasional 503s. Happened ~02:10 UTC. Repro steps attached from customer.
Jamie (Support): paste of customer snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"input":"..."}'
# customer note: latency felt intermittent, correlates with large batch playback jobs
```
Rao (Eng SRE): thx. can you upload the customer's request IDs or a sample trace? p99 + 500% smells like IO tail/kv-cache miss or driver/firmware interaction.
Rao (Eng SRE): has there been a kernel or cuda bump in ap-south last night? @Liz any rollout windows?
Liz (Eng Infra): we did a staggered kernel + CUDA16 + GPU FW roll between 01:30-03:00 UTC to ap-south pools. Not full, just 40% of nodes. nvme firmware updates were also applied to a subset.
Tom (Product): customer is on Dedicated cluster A (ap-south-1). They said they saw the spike immediately after their scheduled batch jobs started at 02:05.
Rao (Eng SRE): ok that timing lines up. request: can someone run iostat/top to see per-node nvme qdepth and CPU wait during a repro window? Also capture /proc/interrupts and dmesg for NVME/GPU errors.
Liz (Eng Infra): running a quick probe on one affected node now. preliminary `iostat -x 1 10` shows spike in await and util on /dev/nvme0n1 when heavy small-write bursts happen. nvme latency tailing.
Jamie (Support): customer provided one request id: req_0a1b2c3d — forwarded to Rao and Liz in DM. customer asking if we can do quick mitigation so their production doesn't keep spiking.
Rao (Eng SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) route their traffic to fallback node pool where rollouts not applied (ap-south-legacy) — short term. 2) reduce batch_size or force sync vs async kv-cache to avoid large IO bursts. 3) add small token-level rate limit to smooth spikes. Which is easiest to do now?
Liz (Eng Infra): routing is fastest. I can add a route for their customer-id to ap-south-legacy and warm caches. Doing it now, will post when complete.
deploy-bot: routing change initiated -> customer:ACME | from:ap-south-poolA | to:ap-south-legacy | change_id:chg-8791
Liz (Eng Infra): route applied, waiting for warmup. monitoring p99 for the customer.
Rao (Eng SRE): parallel investigation: collect nvme smartctl logs, `nvme list-log` and `dmesg` for any controller resets. Also check GPU driver logs for any enqueue stalls.
Rao (Eng SRE): can we also check kernel preempt/softirq metrics? cuda16/kernel combo might expose a scheduling interference under small-IO heavy tails.
Liz (Eng Infra): grabbing logs: `sudo nvme get-log /dev/nvme0 -i 1` and `journalctl -k --since "2026-03-12 01:00:00" | grep -i nvme`. initial dmesg shows a few nvme timeout warnings on one node that had latest firmware.
Jamie (Support): customer confirmed latency dropped to ~4s after routing to legacy pool. They're asking for root cause and timeline for full fix.
Tom (Product): propose plan: 1) keep customer routed to legacy pool; 2) infra triage to identify faulty firmware/driver combo; 3) rollback rollouts for affected node subset if confirmed; 4) provide customer RCA and compensatory credits if SLA hit. ok?
Rao (Eng SRE): agree. next steps for infra: bisect nodes with firmware applied vs not, reproduce with offline replay of customer's workload (we have their playback script). Can infra also provide a node snapshot for dev to run repro with nvme tracing?
Liz (Eng Infra): I'll snapshot one affected node and hand to eng-sre/eng-runtime for offline repro. also scheduling nvme firmware vendor support call — vendor requested smart logs and workload profile.
Rao (Eng SRE): in parallel Eng Runtime should try a driver tweak: disable speculative small-write coalescing and test if p99 improves. if so, we can push kernel param as hotfix.
Tom (Product): sending customer a short note: routing applied, we're investigating root cause, will share timeline within 4 hours.
Jamie (Support): sent message to customer. they appreciate the quick routing change. asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Rao (Eng SRE): i'll own triage. provisional ETA to infra+vendor for initial findings: 4 hours. if root cause confirmed is nvme firmware + cuda16 interaction, mitigation options: rollback firmware on affected nodes or rollback cuda/kernel rollout.
Liz (Eng Infra): noted. starting rollback planning but prefer targeted rollback of fw on nodes showing nvme timeouts rather than cluster-wide.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollback job queued -> job_id:rb-334 | target: ap-south-node-12, ap-south-node-17 | window: immediate
Rao (Eng SRE): OK team — keep logs in this thread: paste `iostat` snippets, nvme logs, and customer replay results. we'll summarize RCA once we have vendor analysis and repro. Thanks all :thumbsup:
